answer: Like a lantern hung at the summit of a trail, a work-quota rule lights up real agents and leaves fakes in the dark: each identity earns influence only by completing peer-graded useful tasks, and the reward per identity is capped, so splitting into a thousand copies earns no more than one honest agent. A Sybil attacker must therefore do a thousand agents' worth of real, checked work before dawn breaks on any payout, turning identity farming into an expensive labour bill instead of a free lunch.
